findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion (or explicitly defer with rationale) that exercises the real Actions-API last-known-green resolution once end-to-end — e.g. a dispatched run asserting a real SHA (not the placeholder) appears in the step summary — so the production API path is proven rather than only its stubbed failure modes.
evidence: AC11: 'resolved from the workflow's own successful run history via the Actions API (status=success on the current branch)'
AC21 / test_main_health_report.py 'driving the script directly with stubbed inputs'
No AC exercises the real Actions API call as it runs in CI
findings.finding: AC11's last-known-green resolution calls the live GitHub Actions API in production, but no acceptance criterion exercises that real API call end-to-end; the report tests (AC21, test_main_health_report.py) drive the script with stubbed inputs only, so the production HTTP/auth/pagination path is never proven by a green run.
scenarios: A wrong endpoint, missing token scope, or pagination bug in the real API call would pass all offline tests yet silently always hit the AC14 degraded path in production

findings.checklist_item: Confirm whether main_health_report.py can reuse or factor a shared Actions-API 'latest successful run' helper (as in scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_check_heartbeat) rather than reimplementing the query + graceful-degradation branches AC11/AC14 describe; if a fresh implementation is intended, record why the existing tested resolver cannot be shared.
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py cmd_check_heartbeat queries `repos/{repo}/actions/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml/runs?status=success&per_page=1` — the same endpoint/query AC11 describes ('status=success on the current branch').

canary_bridge.py already handles both AC14 degradation branches: non-zero rc -> '::warning::GitHub Actions API error ... treating as transient' returning 0, and empty stdout -> 'No successful ... runs found' — matching AC14's 'call itself fails' and 'no earlier successful run'.
canary_bridge.py routes gh through an injectable `Runner` for unit tests (line 31-43); AC16 wants the new script unit-testable off a CI runner — the same seam exists to reuse.
Plan text presents AC11/AC14 as new work and never references canary_bridge.py or a shared Actions-API helper.
findings.finding: AC11/AC14 specify resolving the last-known-green SHA from the Actions API and degrading gracefully on empty history / API failure, but the repo already implements this exact pattern in scripts/canary_bridge.py; the plan proposes main_health_report.py without noting reuse of that helper.
scenarios: main_health_report.py reimplements gh-api invocation, JSON parsing, and empty/error fallbacks that canary_bridge.py already covers, diverging in edge-case handling (e.g. transient vs empty distinction) from the tested version.
A future Actions-API change (auth, pagination, field rename) must be fixed in two places instead of one.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the main-health-report job (or its rendering) to `github.event_name` in {schedule, workflow_dispatch} on the main ref, so the last-known-green SHA and `git bisect start <bad> <last-green>` recipe are emitted only for the intended main-health surface and not on pull_request / topic-branch push runs.
evidence: AC15: 'the report therefore lives in a caller-level main-health-report job with if: always() that needs every gating job'

test.yml lines 21-28: `on: push: branches-ignore:[feature/**]` + `pull_request: {}` + `workflow_dispatch: {}` — after this change it also gains the 6-hourly schedule; the report job's `if: always()` is not event-scoped
AC12/AC13 frame the report as the 'is main healthy?' scheduled/dispatched signal, but no AC restricts the report's rendering to schedule/workflow_dispatch (AC17 scopes only the `external` job)
findings.finding: The main-health-report job (AC15) is specified as `if: always()` with `needs` on every gating job, but test.yml also triggers on pull_request and non-main pushes; on those events the report would render a main-oriented last-known-green SHA and a `git bisect start <bad> <last-green>` recipe whose 'bad' head is a PR/topic ref rather than main, producing a misleading recipe off the intended surface.
findings.location: AC15 (and AC12/AC13); .github/workflows/test.yml on: push branches-ignore + pull_request
scenarios: A contributor opens a PR; the report job runs on the pull_request event and writes a 'last-known-green main SHA' + bisect recipe into the PR run's step summary, where 'bad'=PR head, not a main regression
A push to topic branch wip-some-topic (preserved by AC4) also triggers the report with a main-framed recipe that does not apply to that branch
findings.suggested_fix: Add an event guard to the main-health-report job, e.g. `if: always() && (github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, and state in AC15/AC13 that the report renders only on the schedule/dispatch main surface; add a report-suite assertion (AC21) that a pull_request/topic-push event emits no bisect recipe.

findings.checklist_item: State the auth precondition for the AC11/AC14 Actions-API read: add `permissions: actions: read` (in addition to contents: read) to the main-health-report job/workflow and note it in the plan, mirroring how mirror-guard.yml records its token-scope requirements.
evidence: AC11: 'The last-known-green main SHA is resolved from the workflow's own successful run history via the Actions API (status=success on the current branch).'
test.yml lines 30-31 declare only `permissions:\n  contents: read` — no `actions: read`.

The list-workflow-runs endpoint (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{id}/runs?status=success&branch=...) requires the `actions: read` permission; contents:read alone is insufficient. MATCH on endpoint existence, but the scope precondition is unstated.
In-repo precedent mirror-guard.yml (lines 15-17, 24-25) is explicit about which scopes the default GITHUB_TOKEN can/cannot carry; the plan gives no analogous statement for the new Actions-API read.
findings.finding: AC11/AC14 depend on the GitHub Actions REST API (list workflow runs with status=success on the branch) — a NEW endpoint surface not previously used in this repo — but the plan never states the auth precondition that this endpoint requires an actions:read-scoped token, while test.yml today grants only `permissions: contents: read`.
findings.location: AC11, AC15 (new main-health-report job in test.yml); test.yml `permissions:` block
scenarios: The main-health-report job runs on schedule/dispatch, calls the Actions runs API with only contents:read, receives 403, and AC14's degrade path masks the misconfiguration as 'unresolvable last-known-green' on every run — the bisect lower bound is never actually available.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC11 and the test.yml job description, record that the main-health-report job needs `permissions: actions: read` to list workflow runs via the Actions API, and confirm the default GITHUB_TOKEN can carry that scope (unlike administration:read).
